answer: A work-bonded identity stake makes every new agent post a refundable deposit that unlocks only after crossing a canyon of verified, useful work. A sybil spawning a thousand clones must fund a thousand deposits and wait out the same slow unlock, so its cost scales linearly while its payoff stays near the nadir of zero. Reputation then grows like a willow, bending with signed work receipts, and one failed audit prunes the whole stake, so cloning buys nothing but locked capital.
